description:
## Background

Two prior beads (JMAP-x2gd.52, JMAP-x2gd.53) flagged the same workspace-canonical hot-path-allocation pattern in extension-server reference `MemoryBackend` impls. JMAP-x2gd.84 confirmed the cross-walk: mail-server (canonical) and chat-server carry byte-identical Inner struct shapes that allocate a fresh `String` on every `Inner::current_state`, `bump_state`, `objects_mut`, `objects_ref` call.

## The pattern

```rust
struct Inner {
    objects: HashMap<(&'static str, String), HashMap<Id, Value>>,
    states: HashMap<(&'static str, String), u64>,
    change_log: HashMap<(&'static str, String), Vec<ChangeEntry>>,
    // ...
}

fn objects_ref(&self, type_name: &'static str, account_id: &str)
    -> Option<&HashMap<Id, Value>> {
    self.objects.get(&(type_name, account_id.to_owned()))  // allocates
}
```

Every read constructs a fresh `String` purely to make a temporary tuple key, then drops it after `.get()` returns. Multiplied by every wire-level method call × every JmapObject type the dispatcher routes.

## Sites confirmed

- mail-server memory/mod.rs:109-167 — 6 `.to_owned()` sites at 131, 138, 149, 151, 160, 207 (canonical)
- chat-server memory.rs:80-150 — 6 `.to_owned()` sites at 110, 117, 128, 130, 139, 148 (sibling)

Additional sibling crates (calendars-server, tasks-server, contacts-server, filenode-server, sharing-server, metadata-server) likely carry the same shape — each child bead audits and propagates.

## Design choice (recommended)

JMAP-x2gd.52 enumerates two options:

**(a) Nested HashMap** `HashMap<&'static str, HashMap<String, T>>`. Outer key is `&'static str` (no allocation needed). Inner key is `String` and the standard `Borrow<str>` impl lets `.get(account_id)` work with a `&str` directly without owning. The bead author explicitly recommends this: 'option (a) is the conventional Rust solution and the one a senior Rust practitioner would expect to see in a reference impl.'

**(b) Tuple key with custom Borrow** `HashMap<(&'static str, Box<str>), T>` plus a `Borrow<(&'static str, str)>` impl. Keeps the tuple shape but lets `.get(&("Email", account_id))` skip allocation. More surface area, less conventional.

**This epic adopts option (a).** Rationale:
- Conventional, idiomatic Rust pattern.
- No newtype / Borrow gymnastics that future readers have to decode.
- Inner-map `String` keys interoperate with `Borrow<str>` natively via the stdlib impl.
- Two-step lookup is still O(1) amortized.

## Scope

This epic spans the workspace-wide sweep. Child beads:

1. **${self}.1 — mail-server (CANONICAL)**: restructure Inner. Lands the new shape, helper signatures, and all internal call sites in mail-server. Workspace tests stay green; `MailBackend` trait signatures unchanged (the methods take `&str` already).
2. **${self}.2 — chat-server**: propagate. Mirror the mail-server change byte-for-byte modulo TYPE_NAME constants.
3. **${self}.3 — calendars-server**: propagate.
4. **${self}.4 — tasks-server**: propagate.
5. **${self}.5 — contacts-server**: propagate.
6. **${self}.6 — filenode-server**: propagate (may skip if filenode-server uses a different storage shape — child bead confirms).
7. **${self}.7 — sharing-server**: propagate.
8. **${self}.8 — metadata-server**: propagate.

Each child closes its sibling tracker (`JMAP-x2gd.52` closes when ${self}.2 lands).

## Out of scope

The companion JMAP-x2gd.53 (as-cast pagination casts in `query_objects`) is a separate but related canonical-sweep candidate; a sibling epic will handle that.

## Acceptance criteria

- All seven extension-server `MemoryBackend` Inner structs use the nested-HashMap pattern with no per-call `.to_owned()` on `account_id`.
- `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` green.
- Public trait signatures unchanged (this is an internal storage refactor).
- bd-prime kb note 'memorybackend-objects-mut-silently-auto-registers-accounts-via-known_accounts-insert' continues to hold for the new shape.
